A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLaSMO research, with matching core methods and retained illustrations. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original QED optimization, KAT1 docking simulations, CVAE reconstruction results, and a conditioning ablation.

after.justification: v2 reports original results across 20 optimization tasks, synthetic and retrosynthetic accessibility evaluations, and additional model and optimization analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.3.1 changes the reported GP kernel parameterization from one lengthscale symbol to separate continuous and categorical lengthscales. The BRICS-conditioned CVAE, default architecture, UCB search, similarity constraints, penalties, and Algorithm 1 otherwise remain intact. Newly documented acquisition optimization details do not establish a further procedural change.

E1.justification: The QED and KAT1 docking evaluation becomes a 20-oracle suite covering QED, rediscovery, similarity, multi-property optimization, structural modification, and predicted activity. KAT1 docking results are removed. Appendix A.2 adds training on ZINC250K fragments and mixed QM9/ZINC250K fragments; evaluation also introduces QM9 scaffolds alongside ZINC250K scaffolds.

E2.justification: v1 Table 2 compares against JT-VAE, Scaffold-GGM, DrugHIVE, LIMO, PGFS, and GP-MOLFORMER. v2 Figures 5–7 instead evaluate MARS, Graph-GA, Smiles-GA, Stoned, MolDQN, and SynFlowNet. Earlier methods remaining in related work does not preserve their participation in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces common-scaffold, common-budget baseline comparisons and Top-10 learning curves instead of the earlier maximum/mean QED summaries. The input set becomes 37 QM9 and 63 ZINC250K scaffolds, and the 0.60 similarity threshold disappears. New protocols include baseline tuning, model-dimension comparisons, and SA analysis restricted to settings with at least 30 improved scaffolds.

E4.justification: The QED-only conditioning ablation expands to three oracles and adds random search to isolate LSBO's contribution. New analyses examine fragment sources, latent dimensions, two- versus six-dimensional conditioning, similarity changes, bonding success over iterations, and synthetic accessibility. The earlier training-fragment QED distribution is removed.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies ten seeds, reports seed-averaged bonding rates, and displays error bars on benchmark curves; v1 lacks corresponding repetition and uncertainty reporting. The error-bar statistic is not defined, and neither confidence intervals nor significance tests are specified. This establishes new reporting, not an increase over a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Earlier aggregate QED and KAT1 results are replaced by extensive benchmark and analysis results. For example, v2 Table 1 reports Top-10 QED scores of 0.930, 0.922, and 0.897 for LSBO+CVAE, RS+CVAE, and LSBO+VAE at threshold 0.5. The stated QM9 reconstruction accuracy changes from over 99% to over 90%. Changed metrics and scaffold populations prevent direct performance comparisons with v1.

T1.justification: The kernel definition in Section 4.3.1 now permits separate lengthscales for its continuous and categorical factors, whereas v1 writes both with one parameter. The optimization objectives, CVAE losses, and similarity definition otherwise remain substantively unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion substantially reframe the empirical contribution. The explicit claim of state-of-the-art performance with a significantly smaller model and training dataset is dropped, while broad low-budget optimization performance and maintained synthetic accessibility become central claims. The proposed framework and interactive application contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning additive molecular growth, inability to remove or replace fragments, and unsuitable fixed-size optimization settings. It also explains fragment-size tradeoffs, conditioning-dimensionality effects, declining bonding success, and circumstances favoring MARS. These materially qualify v1's largely positive applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code repository reference, learning rate and scheduler settings, stopping patience, GP hyperparameter fitting, categorical relaxation/rounding, baseline tuning, and scaffold composition details. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation. Conversely, v1's explicit latent search bounds and 100-instance GP initialization are no longer stated.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially around Gao et al.'s sample-efficiency benchmark, strong genetic-algorithm baselines, MARS, GFlowNets/SynFlowNet, STONED, and concurrent GenMol research. SA/RA literature is also introduced. This shifts comparative positioning toward low-budget constrained editing and synthesizability assessment rather than mainly generative-model and scaffold-method comparisons.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is reorganized from separate QED and docking sections into a unified benchmark grouped by task and similarity constraint. Training gains separate dataset-selection and model-training subsections. The abstract, conclusion, and related work are substantially revised, with a dedicated limitations discussion and a reorganized, expanded appendix.

P2.justification: The original QED/docking summaries are replaced by extensive learning-curve grids, SA/RA plots, fragment comparisons, scaffold visualizations, and bonding analyses. Retained content is distinguishable: Figures 1–3 persist, the QED trajectories move from Figure 5 to Figure 8, and the application screenshot moves from Figure 10 to Figure 14.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evidence for comparative sample efficiency and synthesizability through common-budget baseline evaluations, broader ablations, predictive SA/RA checks, and explicit applicability limits. Added implementation details also improve reproducibility. Removing the KAT1 study loses direct docking evidence, and the abstract still mentions docking while error bars remain undefined. These shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial strengthening of the paper's central empirical support.
